analysis:
Examined both test files, their supplied BASE/HEAD evidence, patches and metadata against the canonical definition index. These changes add diagnostic regression tests, not serving controls. StatusCommandRunTests.swift:254–278 requires an unexpired late-renewal grant to remain displayed as App Attest authorization without offering MDM removal. ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests.swift:100–131 separates display lifetime from fresh removal readiness while checking expiry, process/coordinator identity, online status and snapshot freshness; lines 167–207 exercise time boundaries and nonfinite expiry. Lines 224–259 reject missing, mismatched or malformed removal decisions and prevent removal readiness from restoring absent displayed authorization. Existing removal freshness tests remain intact at lines 77–97. Fixtures and the new witness output at line 159 contain synthetic authorization data, not credentials or prompt content.
No concrete regression is supported by these test-only changes. Relevant contracts are A-016/TB-011 and T-052/T-053 (authorization versus evidence and stale grants), T-057 (premature management removal), and T-058 (accurate diagnostics). The surrounding availability, cancellation, cache-guard and billing text tests do not change those controls; no encryption, cache storage or privileged-helper behavior is modified here.
Integration must inspect the implementations of displayedProviderAuthorization/displayedStatus, currentProviderAuthorization/currentStatus and summary, plus changed status/doctor callers and unenroll wiring: confirm the relaxed receipt-age rule is diagnostic-only, removal still requires fresh matching readiness, and connection replacement/revocation invalidates the displayed grant. Those implementations are outside this supplied scope; test expectations alone do not establish enforcement.
